title: Levelwise isomorphisms and complete cones
statement:
Fix the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] on $T_{\Proet}$, with $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and $P_n=A/I^n$. All derived categories of coefficients below are categories of $A_T$-module sheaves, and every finite reduction means $K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, regarded as an $A_T$-module object by restriction of scalars. Derived completeness means that the Koszul completion map of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is an isomorphism.

A morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ whose evaluation at every $n$ is an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism and remains an isomorphism after $\Rlim$. If a derived complete object $C$ satisfies $C\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T=0$ for every $n$, then $C=0$. Consequently a morphism between derived complete objects is an isomorphism once every finite reduction is an isomorphism.

proof.text: First suppose $E_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ has zero evaluation at every level. By [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], evaluation computes kernels and cokernels levelwise. Its termwise derived extension [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] therefore satisfies $\operatorname{ev}_nH^j(E_\bullet)=H^j(\operatorname{ev}_nE_\bullet)=0$. A tower all of whose objects are zero is a zero object: the unique component maps to and from the zero tower commute with transitions and are inverse. Thus all $H^j(E_\bullet)$ vanish. For any complex representing $E_\bullet$, the map from the zero complex is a quasi-isomorphism, hence becomes an isomorphism in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Therefore $E_\bullet=0$.

source.place: First sentence: joint conservativity; zero-object calculation

proof.text: Let $u:M_\bullet\to N_\bullet$ have invertible evaluations. Complete it to a distinguished triangle $(M_\bullet,N_\bullet,E_\bullet)$ using TR1 [def-weil-triangulated-category] in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Exact evaluation, extended as a triangulated functor by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], gives a distinguished triangle at every $n$. By TR3 map the identity triangle on $M_n$ to this triangle, with first two components $1_{M_n},u_n$. The third component $0\to E_n$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], so $E_n=0$. Step 1 gives $E_\bullet=0$. Apply TR3 again from the identity triangle on $M_\bullet$ to the original triangle; its first and third components $1_{M_\bullet},0\to E_\bullet$ are isomorphisms. The same triangle lemma makes the middle component $u$ an isomorphism.

source.place: First sentence: conservative derived evaluations, using cone triangles

proof.text: The functor $\Rlim$ of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] takes an inverse $v$ of the morphism $u$ from step 2 to an inverse: $\Rlim(v)\Rlim(u)=\Rlim(vu)=1$ and $\Rlim(u)\Rlim(v)=1$. It also takes zero objects to zero objects. Indeed it is additive, so the identity of its value on zero is both the identity (functoriality) and the zero endomorphism (additivity). This proves preservation of the isomorphism after $\Rlim$.

source.place: First sentence: the functorial derived inverse limit

proof.text: Let $C$ be derived complete in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. The strict derived quotient tower $C_\bullet$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] evaluates to $C\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, with restriction of scalars to $A_T$. If these objects all vanish, step 1 makes $C_\bullet$ zero, and step 3 makes $\Rlim C_\bullet$ zero. All hypotheses of [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] are those of the fixed adic datum, including Noetherianity and finite perfect quotients. Its last assertion supplies the isomorphism $\operatorname{comp}_C:C\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim C_\bullet$, because the intrinsic Koszul completion map is an isomorphism. Hence $C=0$.

source.place: Second sentence: reconstruction and vanishing of the quotient tower

proof.text: Finally let $u:C\to D$ have complete source and target, and suppose each finite reduction of $u$ is invertible. The derived reduction-tower functor of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] gives $u_\bullet:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ with exactly these evaluations. Steps 2 and 3 make $\Rlim(u_\bullet)$ invertible. By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], $\operatorname{comp}_K=c_K\kappa_K$ is invertible for $K=C,D$. Its naturality gives $\operatorname{comp}_D u=\Rlim(u_\bullet)\operatorname{comp}_C$: the $c_K$ form the stated functorial isomorphism, and $\kappa$ is natural because its maps on representatives are induced by the fixed degree-zero inclusions $A_T[0]\to Q_m$ [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. These inclusions commute with each complex map, hence also with inverses of quasi-isomorphisms in the localization. Thus $u=\operatorname{comp}_D^{-1}\Rlim(u_\bullet)\operatorname{comp}_C$ is a composite of isomorphisms. This establishes the final clause.

source.place: Final sentence: finite-reduction criterion, directly by natural reconstruction

lean.statement: theorem completedAdic_levelwise_isomorphism_cones (T : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A) (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = d.ideal) : (∀ (M N : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicTowers T d)) (u : M ⟶ N), (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso ((completedAdicEvaluation T d n).map u)) → IsIso u ∧ ∀ (RF : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicTowers T d) ⥤ DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules T d)) (η : (lim : CompletedAdicTowers T d ⥤ CompletedAdicModules T d).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RF), RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor η (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (CompletedAdicTowers T d) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) → IsIso (RF.map u)) ∧ (∀ C : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules T d), IsCompletedAdicDerivedComplete T d r a ha C → (∀ n : ℕ, IsZero ((completedAdicFiniteReduction T d n).obj C)) → IsZero C) ∧ (∀ (C D : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules T d)) (u : C ⟶ D), IsCompletedAdicDerivedComplete T d r a ha C → IsCompletedAdicDerivedComplete T d r a ha D → (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso ((completedAdicFiniteReduction T d n).map u)) → IsIso u)

blueprint_update.statement:
A morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$ whose evaluation at every $n$ is
an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism and remains an isomorphism after
$\Rlim$. If a derived complete object $C$ satisfies $C\otimes_A^LP_n=0$ for
every $n$, then $C=0$. Consequently a morphism between derived complete
objects is an isomorphism once every finite reduction is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
The evaluation functors of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] are jointly
conservative on the tower category, and $\Rlim$ is a triangulated functor ([prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]), so
the first assertion holds. For a derived complete $C$,
[prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] identifies $C$ with $\Rlim C_\bullet$,
and the vanishing of every finite reduction kills the tower $C_\bullet$
levelwise, hence $C=0$; the cone of a morphism between derived complete
objects is again derived complete, so the last assertion follows from the
second.
